title: CRASH-004: assignref free container before element use (use-after-free)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: our native ASan build of the pinned 5.0.0 tarball (p12, gcc 15.2.0, libasan from gcc 15, 2026-10-27) reports ASAN:heap-use-after-free at Zend/zend_execute.c:242 in zend_assign_to_variable_reference when trigger.php runs; the corpus records the fix as php-src 4f161fe28997f5d1f818fc6ae95a8131066cf1a2, which postdates the release, and names the defect at Zend/zend_execute.c:242 (UAF read of value_ptr->is_ref); the freeing site is Zend/zend_execute.c:238
fidelity: the corpus's own trigger script, run through the real interpreter (PHP's cli SAPI, ext/standard only, the port's 145 translation units) rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it. The pristine build completes it natively, so an arm that completes it saw nothing.
fault_sites_why: ASan's access stack in our native run (results-ours-asan-default.json, sha256 045e3366bfc5) has zend_assign_to_variable_reference at Zend/zend_execute.c:242 as its first frame inside PHP's tree (frame #0); the stack's remaining frames are the interpreter's dispatch and are not sites

virtual-malloc.oracle: the case on the virtual profile with the nested layer present but returning every freed block's loan, so only musl mallocng revokes, per BLOCK, when PHP's cache hands a block back to free(): a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (tools/arms.json php-real-block)
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: cause=25 pc=0x3fb3c45d68 in zend_assign_to_variable_reference; by function: zend_assign_to_variable_reference at Zend/zend_execute.c:246 is the function this case declares (fault_sites, ASan frame #0 of our native run) (ASan: line 242; a capability fault can land on a neighbouring instruction)

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: the same image with the nested allocator layer retiring the payload at EVERY _efree, cache-absorbed or not, and re-deriving it under a fresh node when the cache hands the block to its next tenant: a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (php-real-object)
virtual-nested-pools.verdict_note: cause=25 pc=0x3fa8845d20 in zend_assign_to_variable_reference; by function: zend_assign_to_variable_reference at Zend/zend_execute.c:242 is the function this case declares (fault_sites, ASan frame #0 of our native run), at ASan's own line

virtual-nested-exact.oracle: virtual-nested-pools with each payload bounded to the caller's request instead of REAL_SIZE(n): the arm that can see a defect inside PHP's own rounding slack (php-real-exact)
virtual-nested-exact.verdict_note: cause=25 pc=0x3fb0045d20 in zend_assign_to_variable_reference; by function: zend_assign_to_variable_reference at Zend/zend_execute.c:242 is the function this case declares (fault_sites, ASan frame #0 of our native run), at ASan's own line

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: the same trigger on stock CheriBSD purecap -- no nested layer at all, the real interpreter cross-built by ports/php/cheribsd/build.sh -- in the boot at the platform default (security.cheri.runtime_revocation_default=1, every_free=0): a SIGPROT at the ASan site with the bounds-malloc control faulting in the same boot, the same binary run with revocation off as the pair that attributes the fault, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (tools/arms.json cheribsd-default)
cheribsd-revocation.verdict_note: reached (route D: PHP printed PHPB_TRIGGER_START from auto_prepend_file, so the interpreter started and entered the trigger) and completed with no fault; NOT-REISSUED: no capability fault at the platform default, but the eager configuration (runtime_revocation_every_free_default=1) faults on this case, so the stale pointer IS followed. The eager fault lands inside the script body, which is what tells a revoked object apart from the allocator's cache being drained back to libc at shutdown. Context, not a verdict: every-free also faults on accesses nothing is meant to catch

status: built 2026-10-27 from the corpus and our native oracle; what has run is in this record's arms (verdict, verdict_from) and under results/
note: population: asan-blind -- ASan reports it only with PHP's allocator patched (cache off, no 8-byte rounding); with zend_alloc.c as shipped the run reads OK. That is the selection, by measurement; which mechanism hides it, and which arm sees it, is what the arms record. Collected by the corpus as carried-from-4.0.2 (historical-known, confidence high).
